# Lab 4.11: Geospatial Analytics

## What We Are Going to Do
Use the GEOGRAPHY type and ST_ functions to measure distance, find points inside an area, and map the results.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Make points and measure distance.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  ST_GEOGPOINT(72.8311, 21.1702) AS surat,
  ST_GEOGPOINT(72.8777, 19.0760) AS mumbai,
  ROUND(ST_DISTANCE(ST_GEOGPOINT(72.8311, 21.1702), ST_GEOGPOINT(72.8777, 19.0760)) / 1000, 1) AS km;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Points are always **(longitude, latitude)**.

2. **[SQL] Stations within 1 km of a point.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT name, ROUND(ST_DISTANCE(ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude), ST_GEOGPOINT(-73.9857, 40.7484))) AS metres
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_stations`
WHERE ST_DWITHIN(ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude), ST_GEOGPOINT(-73.9857, 40.7484), 1000)
ORDER BY metres;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Point-in-polygon join.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab04.stations_by_zip AS
SELECT z.zip_code, COUNT(*) AS stations, ANY_VALUE(z.zip_code_geom) AS geom
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_stations` s
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` z
  ON ST_CONTAINS(z.zip_code_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude))
GROUP BY z.zip_code;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Map the result.** Run `SELECT * FROM lab04.stations_by_zip;`. In the results pane, open the **Visualization** tab, choose the map view, and colour by `stations`.

5. **[CLI] Area and centroid.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT zip_code, ROUND(ST_AREA(geom)/1e6, 2) AS sq_km, ST_ASTEXT(ST_CENTROID(geom)) AS centre
 FROM lab04.stations_by_zip ORDER BY stations DESC LIMIT 5'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Surat → Mumbai | About 232 km in a straight line |
| `ST_DWITHIN` | Stations within 1,000 m |
| `ST_CONTAINS` join | Stations counted per ZIP code |
| Map | Coloured ZIP areas in the results pane |
